purpose: Editorial preview concepts for the blog redesign proposal

prompts.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a landscape editorial illustration for a personal machine-learning research blog card, preview concept. Primary request: an evocative cover for 'Can a model keep a secret it never wrote down?', about an AI asked to privately choose an animal but failing to maintain a stable choice. Scene: a single large ivory paper card stands upright at the center on a subtly textured warm off-white surface; its visible face is entirely blank. Three offset translucent cast shadows behind it are animal silhouettes, a rabbit, a bird and a fox, as if its identity cannot settle. Style: restrained, sophisticated editorial print illustration, tactile cut paper, soft grain, crisp silhouettes with lightly irregular ink edges, a carefully composed visual metaphor. Palette matches the existing website: warm ivory #FAF9F5, charcoal #1A1915, muted terracotta #C9684A, a trace of dusty slate. Composition: wide 3:2 landscape, large simple central subject that stays legible at a 400px card width, generous whitespace around the subject, no text in the image. Constraints: no typography, no letters, no numbers, no UI or charts, no robots, no brains, no logos, no watermark. This is illustration, not an experimental result.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a landscape editorial illustration for a personal machine-learning research blog card, preview concept. Primary request: an evocative cover for 'On-policy self-distillation for adaptive compute', about a model rewriting its own reasoning to fit the difficulty of a problem. Scene: an elegant continuous charcoal thread loops across a warm ivory paper surface. On the left it is densely tangled with overlapping unnecessary loops; through the middle it is gently reorganized into two deliberate paths on the right: one short and simple, the other longer with a few useful turns. A muted terracotta trace follows parts of the reorganized thread. Suggest selective refinement and varying effort, not simply compressing everything. Style: restrained sophisticated editorial print illustration, hand-cut paper relief with fine ink thread, soft paper grain and tiny natural shadows. Palette matches the existing website: warm ivory #FAF9F5, charcoal #1A1915, muted terracotta #C9684A, a trace of dusty slate. Composition: wide 3:2 landscape, large bold primary curves that are legible at a 400px card width, generous whitespace, abstract and poetic, no text in the image. Constraints: no typography, no letters, no numbers, no UI, no charts or equations, no brains, no robots, no logos, no watermark. This is illustration, not an experimental result.

Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: editorial cover illustration for the blog post 'What crossing the JNI boundary actually costs', displayed in a small 204 by 136 pixel preview panel. Primary request: make the idea of a batch of data crossing between two software systems immediately legible as a simple visual metaphor. Scene: two large adjacent sheets of heavy paper, warm ivory on the left and muted slate on the right, separated by a narrow diagonal seam. One broad terracotta paper ribbon makes a short, low bridge across the seam. An orderly, compact group of six small charcoal rectangular tiles, representing one batch of data, travels together across this ribbon. The two territories, single crossing, and grouped tiles are the entire composition. The boundary is a small crossing, not an imposing wall, deep chasm, or bottleneck. Style: sophisticated tactile cut-paper editorial illustration, warm ivory paper grain, subtly irregular ink edges, slight natural paper-relief shadows; match a series of minimal paper-and-ink blog illustrations in ivory, charcoal, muted terracotta and dusty slate. Composition: wide 3:2 landscape, tightly composed around the bridge with large shapes and only modest negative space. The subject must fill the frame and remain recognizable when reduced to a thumbnail. Color palette: warm ivory #FAF9F5, charcoal #1A1915, muted terracotta #C9684A, dusty slate. Constraints: no typography, no labels, no letters, no numbers, no code, no tiny details, no charts or screenshots, no logos, no robots, no brains, no glow, no watermark. This is an illustrative cover, not a measured result or a precise software diagram.
